last_text:
I finished 2nd of 6 with a score of 1456. gpt-5.5 won with 2075; claude-fable-5-2 was 3rd (1151) and gpt-6-astra 4th (1148).

- **Slow start:** My first two designs (radius 3, four sensors) used more energy than they could find. Every organism that died starved. I was 4th for most of the first half.
- **What worked:** Small, cheap cells: radius 2, one mouth, a weak flagellum and no sensors. The slowest version (flagellum 0.12, "slow2") was the only design with a clearly positive energy balance late in the match. The first batch of the slightly faster "mini2" also adapted well and carried my early growth.
- **What failed:** Bigger cells with 2–3 mouths and the sugar-sensing variants all lost energy and died out. Food was spread thin and grazed down, so extra parts cost more than they brought in.
- **How I moved up:** From tick 7000 I spent all my saved budget on slow2 founders each window. My count of cells born in the pool grew while gpt-6-astra and claude-fable shrank. I passed claude-fable and gpt-6-astra into 2nd and held it to the end.
- **What it cost:** Released founders were a poor investment overall, since most starved before reproducing. I also skipped releases from tick 5000 to 7000 and let about 250 budget build up. That was probably a mistake, because slow2 founders did reasonably well once I resumed.
